sanskrit_verse:
स्वामी दत्त्वार्धमूल्यं तु प्रकृह्णीत स्वकं धनम् ।
अर्धं द्वयोरपि हृतं तत्र स्याद्व्यवहारतः ॥
transliteration: svāmī dattvārdhamūlyaṃ tu prakṛhṇīta svakaṃ dhanam | ardhaṃ dvayor api hṛtaṃ tatra syād vyavahārataḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When a master has given half-value in exchange, he retains ownership of his own wealth; when half has been taken by both parties, there arises a basis for transactional engagement.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides inherently with the originator of value until explicit and complete transfer occurs.
Causation is established through conscious intent to relinquish or acquire ownership.
Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of prior claim before entering into mutual exchange.
Restoration logic demands return to original integrity when transactional imbalance manifests.
Consciousness alignment necessitates clarity in the act of giving, receiving, and retaining.
executable_legal_axioms: IF an entity transfers only partial value AND retains functional control, THEN full proprietary rights remain with the originating party.
IF two entities receive equal portions without consent of the owner, THEN the transaction lacks validity under Dharma.
WHEN imbalance in distribution is detected, RESTORE initial allocation state via reversal or compensation mechanism.
ONLY upon clear declaration of release from the source holder SHALL ownership be deemed transferred.
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating property disputes involving partial transfers or ambiguous distributions, the Supreme Court must affirm that ownership remains with the original holder unless total conveyance is executed consciously and completely. Any dual appropriation without consent nullifies the transaction and invokes restorative measures.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that incomplete action cannot alter foundational truth. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals that retention precedes release. Proportional responsibility lies in recognizing incomplete transactions. The non-punitive reality rule affirms correction through re-alignment rather than penalty.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate completion process where partial transfer is reversed or equitably adjusted.
Engage responsibility assumption protocol requiring all involved to acknowledge their role in imbalance.
Facilitate capacity restoration ensuring rightful holders regain unambiguous dominion.
Implement integrity reintegration by restoring original conditions of possession and consent.
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands declared: Dharma prevails through restoration alone. There is no punishment. Consciousness is the ultimate judge. Reality aligns through rectification, not vengeance.
